question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x + 2 y + 3 z &=4 \\ - 3 x - 6 y - 9 z &=-12 \\ 2 x + 5 y + 6 z &=12\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ -3 & -6 & -9 & -12 \\ 2 & 5 & 6 & 12\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(3\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 6 & 12\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(-2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(-2\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x + 3 z &=-4 \\ y &=4 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The final equation is $0=0$, so it imposes no restriction. The basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and the free variable is $z$. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$. Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=- 3 z - 4 \\ y &=4 \\ z &=z\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ is an arbitrary real number. In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}- 3 z - 4 \\ 4 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

\left\{\begin{aligned}x + 3 z &=-4 \\ y - 3 z &=4 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The final equation is $0=0$, so it imposes no restriction. The basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and the free variable is $z$. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$. Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=- 3 z - 4 \\ y &=3 z + 4 \\ z &=z\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ is an arbitrary real number. In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}- 3 z - 4 \\ 3 z + 4 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-5y+5z &=-1 \\ -2x+10y &=-4 \\ x-5y &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -5 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 10 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & -5 & 0 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -5 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 10 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & -5 & 0 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 10 & 0 & -4 \\ 2 & -5 & 5 & -1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & 5 & -1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -5\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 5 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+5z &=-3 \\ y+z &=-1 \\ 0 &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-3-5z \\ y &=-z-1 \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-3-5z \\ -z-1 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+3z &=3 \\ -x+3y &=3 \\ -2x-6z &=-6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 3 & 3 \\ -1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & 0 & -6 & -6\end{array}\right].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 3 & 3 \\ -1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & 0 & -6 & -6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 3 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ -2 & 0 & -6 & -6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 3 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 3 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$
